# `Q-16-12` — Engine failed to load while answering a claim

> Quarto had to start an engine extension to ask whether it handles a
> language or file, and the engine failed to load.

## What this means

An engine that decides what it handles at run time (see
[`Q-16-10`](Q-16-10.qmd)) has to be running before Quarto can ask it
anything. This warning means starting it failed — a syntax error in the
bundle, a missing import, a module that throws on load.

Quarto treats the unanswered question as **"not claimed"** and keeps
going. That choice keeps a broken engine from taking down the whole
render, but it means the failure shows up somewhere else, disguised:

- **A code cell is not executed.** No engine claimed the language, so
  the cell is written to the output as a plain code block. The page
  renders, and the code appears verbatim instead of its results.
- **A file reports no engine.** If the failed engine was the one that
  would have claimed a `.ipynb` or similar input, you get
  `Can't determine execution engine for <file>` — which points at
  configuration, when the real cause was the load failure.

This warning exists so the real cause is visible. It carries the
underlying load error.

## How to fix

Start with the error text in the message — it comes from the engine's
own module and usually names the failing import or statement directly.

Then:

1. **Rebuild the engine bundle.** A stale or partially-written
   `dist/*.js` is the most common cause. Run the extension's build step
   (for TypeScript engines, `q2 call build-ts-extension` in the
   extension directory).
2. **Check the bundle exists and is complete** at the `path` named in
   the extension's `_extension.yml`.
3. **Load it directly** to see the failure without Quarto in the way:
   `deno run --allow-all <path-to-bundle>`.

If you do not maintain the extension, report the error to its author.

## Why the render still succeeds

Claim answering has to be infallible — it runs while Quarto is deciding
what to do, before any document is committed to an engine. Making a load
failure fatal there would mean one broken extension prevents a project
from rendering at all, even for documents that never touch it.

So the failure is reported and the render continues. Use `--strict` if
you would rather this stop the build:

```bash
q2 render --strict
```
